system.name: Databricks Genie
system.version: Genie conversations API (Space grounded on the 22 base tables), databricks-sdk 0.136.0

cost_usd_per_task.unavailable_reason: Genie bills DBUs against the serving warehouse and the conversations API returns no per-request usage, so no per-task figure is derivable. The run metered 855.8 DBU of GENIE_FREE_USAGE (Genie itself is on the free tier) plus 61.4 DBU of billable serverless SQL compute across all 570 executions; that is warehouse uptime, not per-task cost, and dividing it by 570 would invent a number. Snowflake Cortex Analyst is recorded the same way.

declarations.artifacts: databricks_agent/captures/genie_captures_run{1,2,3}.jsonl (149 single-turn) and genie_captures_mt_run{1,2,3}.jsonl (41 multi-turn turns), concatenated to genie_captures_190_run{1,2,3}.jsonl. Each row carries the question, Genie's SQL, the returned columns/types/rows, latency, conversation_id and the timeout in force. runs/genie_answer_run{1,2,3}.jsonl are the decoded answers, runs/genie_answer_sub{1,2,3}.json the submissions, runs/genie_answer_3run_score/ the verdicts.
declarations.notes: COMMERCIAL BAND: Genie is a managed product bringing its own undisclosed model, so this is NOT a scaffold comparison against the four controlled arms, which all run gpt-5.6-luna. It belongs with Claude Code and Snowflake Cortex Analyst. ANSWER-TRACK, AND THIS ROW IS THE BOARD'S ONE EXCEPTION: every other arm is SQL-track -- the harness re-executes the agent's SQL on the single reference warehouse. This row is scored on the rows GENIE'S OWN warehouse returned, with nothing re-executed. That is only valid if the Databricks tables hold the data gold was computed from, so it was proved before any metered call: all 22 tables present, every row count exact (58,463,766 total), every column set matching, and 1,238 per-column aggregates (COUNT, COUNT DISTINCT, SUM, MIN, MAX) identical on both engines. The SQL-track was then computed from the SAME captures as a cross-check and lands at 115/190 against answer-track's 117/190 -- a 2-task, 1.1pp difference, which is the evidence that the load is faithful and the two methods agree. The SQL-track figure required adding one dialect rule (try_divide, which DuckDB lacks); before it, 63 statements that ran correctly on Databricks failed on DuckDB, and the cross-check would have measured the shim's coverage rather than the agent. DECODING: the Databricks SQL API returns every cell as a string, so values are decoded to native types using the column types Databricks reported in the same response. Nothing is rounded, reinterpreted or repaired; a cell that will not decode is left verbatim and allowed to fail. An executed query returning zero rows is submitted as the empty set, not as a missing answer -- 9 of the 10 tier-7 negative controls have the empty set as gold, and conflating the two would fail them. MULTI-TURN IS CHAINED THROUGH GENIE'S OWN CONVERSATION: turn 1 opens a conversation and every later turn is sent to that same conversation_id, so the agent carries its own context exactly as a user would experience it. No authored gold prior is ever substituted. Threading was verified intact across all 24 captured sessions. TIME LIMIT: 180 s per question, passed explicitly into the SDK and recorded on every row. This matters -- databricks-sdk's *_and_wait helpers default to a 1200 s timeout, so an unset value would have given Genie 6.7x the budget every other arm runs under. CAPTURE HEALTH: 570/570 executions recorded with status ok, zero retries, zero truncation, zero auth failures, zero rate-limit backoffs; 570/570 produced SQL. RE-CAPTURE DISCLOSED: in the first pass, four turns of one 9-turn session timed out when the capture host entered macOS Maintenance Sleep mid-call (confirmed by pmset, and by wall-clock elapsed exceeding measured latency by 14-53 minutes while time.monotonic stalled). Those were not Genie failures. That whole session was discarded and re-captured as a single clean conversation with sleep inhibited; the re-capture moved Pass^3 from 115 to 117 and tier-9 from 17 to 19. No other execution in the run was affected. ROW CAP: stored result rows are capped at 100,000, matching the Snowflake arm. An earlier 1,000 cap sat below the largest gold answer in the corpus (1,322 rows, Set-Match) and would have truncated and failed that task while uncapped arms got a fair attempt.
